query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: seat_product_downgrade
per_column.rationale: Captures whether the flown seat product matched the expected Business-Class product (qsuite/flat_bed delivered) versus a downgrade with/without notice. This is a concrete candidate CAUSE whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed. The query only says 'Business-Class'; it does not name a seat downgrade / Qsuite-vs-flatbed distinction, so this is surfaced from the data.

per_column.name: aircraft_age_and_condition
per_column.rationale: Aircraft age/condition plausibly drives BOTH the seat product actually installed/delivered (older frames less likely to carry the newest Qsuite, more prone to 'downgrade') AND passenger satisfaction/recommendation directly (degraded, worn cabins depress ratings). That makes it a genuine common cause that must be adjusted for, and it is not mentioned in the query.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A parallel/competing cause of the outcome (poor crew service lowers recommendation) but it does NOT cause the seat-product treatment, so it is not a common cause / confounder of that treatment. It is not on the treatment->outcome path either, so not a mediator. Treated as an alternative driver.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Another independent determinant of recommendation. It does not cause a seat-product downgrade, so it is not a confounder of the treatment, and a seat downgrade does not cause food quality, so it is not a mediator. A parallel outcome-driver.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_legs
per_column.rationale: Encodes single-leg vs multi-leg and whether service was consistent/variable. This is closer to a downstream summary of the service experience (mediator/outcome-like) or a structural covariate than a clean common cause of the seat-downgrade treatment. Only weakly a confounder, so classified as other.

per_column.name: ffp_elite_status_handling
per_column.rationale: Whether frequent-flyer elite status was recognised/handled can plausibly affect BOTH treatment allocation (elites less likely to be silently downgraded, more likely upgraded/accommodated) AND propensity to recommend (better-handled elites rate higher; mishandled ones churn). A plausible, though weakly supported (mostly false), common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The set does establish a causal-estimation frame: seat_product_downgrade is a well-defined treatment (candidate cause of non-recommendation) and at least one column, aircraft_age_and_condition, is a genuine common cause of BOTH that treatment (older frames -> different/downgraded seat product) and the outcome (degraded cabin -> lower recommendation), surfaced from data rather than the query. ffp_elite_status_handling is a further, weaker but plausible confounder also not named in the query. However, the majority of the added columns (cabin_crew_service_quality, food_beverage_quality, service_consistency_across_legs) are parallel/competing outcome drivers rather than common causes of the treatment, so the design leans toward driver enumeration rather than a clean confounder-adjustment set. Because a real, non-copied confounder is present but the confounder set is diluted by non-confounders, confounder_quality is moderate (0.55).
